2.5 Exercises 2- Exercises on groups (S) Question 2.5.1. Let G be a group with g, h ∈ G. Prove that, for all n ∈ N, (g−1hg) n = g−1hng. Question 2.5.2. [Warning! Really easy proofs — don’t overthink this.] Let G be a group and H ≤ G. (a) Prove that ∣H∣ = 1 if and only if H = ⟨eG⟩. (b) Suppose ∣G∣ is finite. Prove that ∣H∣ = ∣G∣ if and only if H = G. (c) Is the statement in (b) true if ∣G∣ is infinite? Question 2.5.3. Let G be a group with H ≤ G and K ≤ G. Prove that H ∩ K ≤ G. Question 2.5.4. Let G be a finite group and g ∈ G. Prove that ∣⟨g⟩∣ = o(g). Question 2.5.5. Let g ∈ S10 be the permutation g = (1 3 5 7)(2 4). Write down all the elements in the following. (a) ⟨g⟩ (b) ⟨g2⟩ Question 2.5.6. Show that for all n ∈ N, the group Zn is cyclic, with Zn = ⟨[1]n⟩.
